title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1981 study of maps (cartes) and dessins as covers of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, here in the real, non-oriented setting. On the previous page he set up a fully faithful functor (26) from finite weighted triangular maps (cartes triangulaires pondérées) of type {0,1,∞}, not necessarily oriented, to finite étale covers X' of the R-scheme P^1_R − {0,1,∞}. Such covers are the same as ramified covers of P^1_R that are étale over U_{0,3,R}. The essential image is characterised by condition (27): X'(R) = ∅.

This page describes the inverse functor:
- Take the Riemann surface X'(C).
- Pull back the real line P^1(R) ⊂ P^1(C). This gives an oriented triangulation of X'(C). Its vertex set is the fibre over {0,1,∞}, and it is partitioned by type 0, 1, ∞, which is the 'particularisation'.
- Pass to the quotient by complex conjugation τ.

Because X'(R) = ∅, the involution τ acts freely, so X'(C)/τ is a closed surface without boundary, possibly non-orientable, carrying the descended triangulation. This is the non-oriented map.

If (27) is dropped, (28) X = X'(C)/τ is a compact surface with boundary (a Klein surface carrying a dianalytic/conformal structure). The boundary is the image of the real points. Grothendieck remarks that the definition of weighted triangular maps extends, in an evidently unique way, from compact surfaces without boundary to compact surfaces with boundary, so that (26) becomes an equivalence of categories. In modern terms this is a real Belyi theorem: all real covers of P^1_R − {0,1,∞}, equivalently real algebraic curves with a real Belyi map, correspond to dessins on compact Klein surfaces, possibly with boundary.

Section 4 then begins: on a map (oriented or not) one can impose relations (29) ρ_i^{ν_i} = 1 with ν_i ∈ N* in the cartographic group. The next page explains that this means the vertices of type i have valency/order dividing ν_i. In modern language these are maps or hypermaps of type (ν_0, ν_1, ν_∞), i.e. quotients of (extended) triangle groups, or covers of the orbifold P^1 with signature (ν_0, ν_1, ν_∞).
errors: The machine transcription has 'ce qui donne une surface à bord, grâce à la condition (27)'. Mathematically it must be 'sans bord': (27) makes τ act freely, so the quotient has no boundary. The image is consistent with 'sans'. Likewise the extension should be from surfaces compactes SANS bord to surfaces compactes À bord.

No genuine mathematical errors. The phrase 'de façon évidemment unique' hides some care needed at boundary vertices and edges, namely how half-edges and the weights behave on the fixed locus of τ. Grothendieck does not spell this out.

ideas.what: Non-oriented (weighted triangular) maps of type {0,1,∞} are equivalent to finite étale covers of P^1_R − {0,1,∞} with no real points. The inverse functor is X' ↦ X'(C)/τ with the triangulation pulled back from P^1(R).
ideas.modern_name: Real Belyi theory / dessins d'enfants on non-orientable surfaces; Klein surfaces and real algebraic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Köck & Singerman, 'Real Belyi theory' (2007); also Jones–Singerman on non-orientable hypermaps
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), where non-oriented maps are discussed; unsure of an explicit statement

ideas.what: Extension of the notion of map to compact surfaces with boundary, so that the functor becomes an equivalence with ALL real covers of P^1_R − {0,1,∞}, i.e. dropping X'(R) = ∅.
ideas.modern_name: Maps/dessins on surfaces with boundary (Klein surfaces), NEC groups, extended triangle groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bryant & Singerman, 'Foundations of the theory of maps on surfaces with boundary' (1985); Köck–Singerman (2007) for the real-curve equivalence

ideas.what: Imposing relations ρ_i^{ν_i} = 1 in the cartographic group to restrict the valencies of vertices of type i.
ideas.modern_name: Maps/hypermaps of type (ν_0, ν_1, ν_∞); quotients of triangle groups; orbifold covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones & Singerman (1978); Coxeter–Moser earlier for regular maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the cartographic group and triangle groups in related terms

missed.claim: As early as 1981, Grothendieck formulated the real Belyi correspondence. Non-oriented maps correspond to covers of P^1_R − {0,1,∞} without real points. Maps on compact surfaces with boundary give an equivalence with all such real covers. This predates Bryant–Singerman (1985) on maps with boundary and Köck–Singerman's 'Real Belyi theory' (2007), which do not credit him.
missed.quote: on pourrait étendre (de façon évid. unique) la définition des cartes triangulaires pondérées sur des surfaces compactes sans bord, au cas des surfaces compactes à bord, de telle façon que (26) devienne une équivalence de catégories
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical priority. It shows that the real/Galois-over-R aspect of dessins (action of Gal(C/R) and non-orientable maps) was integral to Grothendieck's original program, not a later add-on. The result itself is now in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The statement is correct and somewhat ahead of the published literature (Bryant–Singerman 1985, Köck–Singerman 2007). However, it is a natural consequence of the oriented Belyi–Grothendieck correspondence plus descent from C to R, and specialists would find it unsurprising in substance; the interest is historical precedence.
transcription_corrections: 'ce qui donne une surface à bord, grâce à la condition (27)' should read 'ce qui donne une surface sans bord, grâce à la condition (27)'.

'la définition des cartes pures[?] triangulaires pondi-ées[?] sur des surfaces compactes à bord, au cas des surfaces compactes à bord' should read approximately 'la définition des cartes triangulaires pondérées sur des surfaces compactes sans bord, au cas des surfaces compactes à bord'. The interlinear word above 'triangulaires' is probably 'finies'.
'(Bet.B.4[?])' at the top is a crossed-out archival/page label, not mathematics.
'[-ou-] où ν_i ∈ N*' is likely 'avec ν_i ∈ N*' (struck word) followed by 'qui signifie donc que'.
